hotspots.label: Ground nest
hotspots.fact: Dodos laid a single egg in a nest on the ground, so anything that walked by could eat it.

hotspots.label: Grey feather
hotspots.fact: The dodo was a giant flightless pigeon. Its closest living relative is the Nicobar pigeon.

hotspots.label: Ship rat
hotspots.fact: Ships brought rats, pigs and monkeys to Mauritius. They raided dodo nests.

hotspots.label: Felled ebony tree
hotspots.fact: Settlers cut down Mauritius's ebony forests for timber, shrinking the dodo's habitat.

hotspots.label: Dutch sailor
hotspots.fact: Dutch sailors reached Mauritius in 1598. The dodo had never met humans and wasn't afraid of them.

hotspots.label: Old bones
hotspots.fact: The last widely accepted sighting of a dodo was in 1662, less than 70 years after humans arrived.

threats.name: Hunting
threats.description: Sailors kill fearless dodos for food.

threats.name: Invasive species
threats.description: Rats, pigs and monkeys eat eggs and chicks.

threats.name: Deforestation
threats.description: Forests are cleared for timber and farms.

threats.name: Cyclones
threats.description: Rare cyclones hit the island hard.

interventions.name: Pest control
interventions.description: Trap invasive rats and pigs near nesting grounds.

interventions.name: Hunting ban
interventions.description: Ban hunting dodos on the island.

interventions.name: Forest reserve
interventions.description: Protect a block of native forest.
